v.why: With edge 0 removed node 1 receives no input, so edge 2 carries nothing and a conv there cannot change accuracy.
Edge 0 only matters through edges 2 and 4, so when edge 4 is none the conv has fewer routes to the output.
Node 2 feeds the output only through edge 5, so a conv on edge 1 is a dead end when edge 5 is none.
A skip on edge 1 feeds node 2 a clean signal that a live conv on edge 5 can transform, whereas with edge 5 none the skip is wasted.
Adding the direct input-to-output shortcut where there was none gives a large gradient-flow gain, unlike replacing an existing op.
A conv on the direct edge already gives a strong path to the output, so another parallel conv shows saturation.
A 1x1 conv on edge 3 overlaps with an existing 1x1 conv path into node 3, so the gain is smaller.
Removing the identity shortcut hurts more than removing other ops because it takes away the easiest gradient path.
An identity on edge 0 passes the input cleanly into a live conv on edge 2, whereas with edge 2 none it has fewer routes.
Replacing a conv on the final edge with pooling reduces capacity, so it is worse than adding pooling to an empty or skip edge.
